section_summary: This section chiefly documents applications, military clearances, and travel-document requirements for diplomats, missionaries, commercial representatives, shipbuilding inspectors, and other foreign entrants to occupied Japan. It also covers Venezuelan and Chinese diplomatic or commercial travel, José Teruya’s proposed repatriation from Okinawa to Peru, diplomatic representation in Japan, and immigration inquiries concerning Anna Slenkina and V. N. Shepitkovsky. Recurring issues include SCAP sponsorship procedures, valid passports or identity documents, re-entry permits, passport photographs, and waivers of U.S. exit permits.

subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 3: memorandum for record on Soviet clearance and security
subfiles.about: Reviews SCAP authority to inspect Soviet personnel and fragmentary concerns about defectors and Soviet security activity.
subfiles.summary: Major General Willoughby recalls that mission-head certification once substituted for inspection of Soviet travelers, but later abuse prompted normal inspections except for bona fide diplomats. The damaged concluding material mentions defectors, the Russian secret police, Communists, and a kidnapping.

subfiles.title: Recommendation for Reverend Victor Mroz
subfiles.about: Recommends Victor Mroz for a military permit to enter Japan as a Catholic missionary.
subfiles.summary: The Apostolic Delegate guarantees that Mroz will not burden Japan or the occupation forces or undertake unauthorized activities.

subfiles.title: Application of Johannes Julius Mendelsohn to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Johannes Julius Mendelsohn; J. Gerber & Co.
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Requests commercial entry to reorganize prewar export trade involving Japan, South Africa, and the Belgian Congo.
subfiles.summary: Mendelsohn applies for a six-month commercial visit and identifies banking, business, travel, and proposed itinerary information.

subfiles.title: Explanation for Mrs. Mendelsohn’s accompanying travel
subfiles.from: J. J. Mendelsohn, J. Gerber & Co.
subfiles.about: Explains that Mendelsohn’s wife would serve as his confidential secretary and Japanese interpreter.
subfiles.summary: Mendelsohn states that the couple lived in Japan from 1934 to 1946 and that his wife regularly assisted his work.

subfiles.title: Corporate support for Mendelsohn’s Japan application
subfiles.from: G. A. Griesbach, J. Gerber & Co.
subfiles.about: Supports Mendelsohn’s trip to rebuild Japanese export trade with Africa.
subfiles.summary: The company identifies Mendelsohn as its vice president and former head of a leading Kobe exporter to Africa.

subfiles.title: Application of William J. Molson to visit Japan
subfiles.from: William J. Molson; State Export Company
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks entry to establish a Japanese office for imports to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Molson proposes a one-month visit to Tokyo, Yokohama, and Osaka to develop the company’s import business.

subfiles.title: Forwarding note concerning José Teruya
subfiles.to: American Embassy, Lima, through the Department of State
subfiles.about: Forwards a letter to José Teruya’s mother about his repatriation from Okinawa to Peru.
subfiles.summary: Transmits the enclosed explanatory consular letter at the embassy’s discretion.

subfiles.title: Letter to Ushi vda. de Teruya concerning her son
subfiles.from: James B. Pilcher, American Consul General
subfiles.about: Explains what Peruvian authorization is required before José Teruya can return from Okinawa.
subfiles.summary: Pilcher says no official Peruvian approval or travel documentation has reached the United States through diplomatic channels. He suggests contacting Peru’s Foreign Ministry and promises prompt assistance once approval arrives.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Nicholson File Company
subfiles.about: Postmarked envelope associated with A. E. Small’s correspondence.
subfiles.summary: Providence envelope addressed to the Secretary of State.

subfiles.title: Acknowledgment of A. E. Small’s military permit
subfiles.about: Acknowledges Military Permit No. 5203 and gives planned sailing details.
subfiles.summary: Small plans to sail from San Francisco aboard the President Cleveland on November 7 and notes that no U.S. exit permit is required.

subfiles.title: Lebanese Legation note requesting a new permit for Michel Chami
subfiles.about: Requests renewal of Michel Chami’s unused permission to enter Japan.
subfiles.summary: The legation explains that Chami could not use his December 1948 authorization and now seeks a replacement military permit.

subfiles.title: Entry action slip for Michel J. Chami
subfiles.about: Clears Chami for indefinite entry between October 25, 1949, and April 25, 1950, subject to documentation.
subfiles.summary: Clearance requires photographs, a valid travel document, and permission to re-enter another country.

subfiles.title: Referral of Michel Chami’s application to the Army
subfiles.about: Requests SCAP consideration of Chami’s business-travel application.
subfiles.summary: Chappell forwards the Lebanese Legation’s application in duplicate and asks to be informed of SCAP’s decision.

subfiles.title: Department memorandum approving Michel Chami’s entry
subfiles.about: Notifies the legation of Chami’s conditional clearance and passport-endorsement procedure.
subfiles.summary: Chami may enter Japan between October 25, 1949, and April 25, 1950, for an indefinite stay if he has onward-entry permission and two photographs. The legation is asked to arrange the SCAP clearance statement in his passport and receives two commercial-entrant guides.

subfiles.title: Reference slip to Mr. Krieg
subfiles.about: Internal Department of State routing slip with a brief handwritten instruction.
subfiles.summary: Restricted reference slip routing material to Mr. Krieg.

subfiles.title: Hong Kong telegram concerning José Miztel Ferrera
subfiles.about: Asks whether SCAP should reconsider refusing temporary entry to Venezuela’s chargé at Canton.
subfiles.summary: Ferrera seeks roughly one month in Japan while awaiting Venezuelan instructions; Hong Kong asks whether to notify him of refusal or seek reconsideration.

subfiles.title: Peiping telegram supporting Chuang Pao-ching’s Japan visit
subfiles.to: Secretary of State; Tokyo for information
subfiles.about: Strongly recommends facilitating Chuang’s commercial trip to Japan for political and economic reasons.
subfiles.summary: Clubb details Hua Feng’s substantial China–Japan trade and argues that enabling Chuang and Chin to visit Japan would encourage non-Soviet commercial ties.

subfiles.title: Relay of Peiping telegram 1745 to SCAP
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Relays Peiping’s recommendation regarding Chuang Pao-ching and Chin Ting-chih.
subfiles.summary: Orders the text of Peiping telegram 1745 repeated to the acting political adviser.

subfiles.title: Request to reconsider Ferrera’s entry
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Urges reconsideration of Ferrera’s proposed one-month stay in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Department invokes good-neighbor relations with Venezuela and directs repetition to Hong Kong.

subfiles.title: Tokyo reply on sponsorship of Chuang Pao-ching
subfiles.about: Explains the sponsorship process and says SCAP cannot approve Chuang’s entry without it.
subfiles.summary: Hong Kong-domiciled Chinese traders require Chamber of Commerce and colonial-government approval followed by sponsorship from the United Kingdom liaison mission in Tokyo. Chuang’s application lacked that sponsorship.

subfiles.title: Memorandum on Brazilian and Iranian diplomatic representation
subfiles.about: Reports changes and uncertainties concerning Brazilian and Iranian diplomatic missions in Japan.
subfiles.summary: Portugal ceased protecting Brazilian interests after Brazil opened its mission; theater headquarters knew of no Iranian representative traveling to establish one.

subfiles.title: Commerce transmittal for Joseph I. Goldman
subfiles.from: Department of Commerce, Far Eastern Branch
subfiles.about: Forwards Commerce’s approval of Goldman’s proposed commercial travel to Japan.
subfiles.summary: Goldman’s application remains subject to final SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Application of Joseph I. Goldman to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Joseph I. Goldman; American Nile Corporation
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks a three-month trip to buy silk and cotton goods for U.S. and Middle Eastern markets.
subfiles.summary: The Egyptian representative proposes traveling from Cairo to Tokyo, Osaka, and Kobe and lists corporate and banking information.

subfiles.title: Certification of Goldman’s Egyptian documentation
subfiles.about: Confirms Goldman’s Egyptian residence, passport, and re-entry permit.
subfiles.summary: The company supplies Goldman’s passport number, issue date, validity, and Egyptian re-entry status.

subfiles.title: Duplicate Commerce transmittal for Goldman
subfiles.from: Milton A. Berger, Department of Commerce
subfiles.about: Again transmits Commerce approval of Goldman’s application, subject to SCAP.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate notice of Goldman’s approved commercial-travel application.

subfiles.title: Commerce list of four approved commercial travelers
subfiles.from: Department of Commerce, Far Eastern Branch
subfiles.about: Lists Hamway, Rie, Kaptzan, and Flitterman as Commerce-approved Japan travelers.
subfiles.summary: Forwards four applications for final SCAP approval.

subfiles.title: Referral concerning Aslaksen and Dahl
subfiles.about: Asks the Pacific Military Permit Branch to act on the cases of two shipbuilding inspectors.
subfiles.summary: Chappell forwards the company’s explanatory letter concerning J. Boe Aslaksen and Torger Dahl.

subfiles.title: Envelope from Naess, Mejlaender & Co.
subfiles.to: Walter F. Chappell, Department of State
subfiles.about: Air-mail envelope accompanying the company’s application for two inspectors.
subfiles.summary: New York envelope addressed to Chappell at the Department of State.

subfiles.title: Application for permits for J. Boe Aslaksen and Torger Dahl
subfiles.from: Kurth O. Skulstad, Naess, Mejlaender & Co.
subfiles.about: Requests permits for two Norwegian inspectors supervising a cargo liner’s construction at Yokohama.
subfiles.summary: Aslaksen and Dahl are to remain through completion of an 8,500-ton vessel expected in late 1950. The company says SCAP approved owner inspection and asks for expedited permits.

subfiles.title: National Catholic Welfare Conference application for Victor Mroz
subfiles.about: Submits Mroz’s permit application and explains his displaced-person documentation.
subfiles.summary: The Polish Franciscan is being sent from Hartland to Nagasaki and travels on an affidavit of identity because his home area is under Russian control.

subfiles.title: Apostolic Delegate’s supporting letter for Victor Mroz
subfiles.about: Recommends Mroz for missionary entry and guarantees his support and conduct.
subfiles.summary: Duplicate supporting letter for Mroz’s military-permit application.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Military Permit No. 5327 to Victor Mroz
subfiles.about: Sends Mroz’s military permit for entry between October 26 and December 26, 1949.
subfiles.summary: Mohler is asked to deliver Permit No. 5327 to Father Mroz.

subfiles.title: Request for SCAP consideration of Victor Mroz
subfiles.about: Forwards Mroz’s application and supporting letters for SCAP review.
subfiles.summary: Chappell requests theater consideration and issuance of a military permit if clearance is granted.

subfiles.title: Conditional clearances for Flitterman, Hamway, and Kaptzan
subfiles.about: Reports theater clearance for three commercial entrants, subject to onward-entry documentation.
subfiles.summary: Military permits will issue after proof of valid travel documents and re-entry permission elsewhere.

subfiles.title: Application of M. E. Kaptzan to visit Japan
subfiles.from: M. E. Kaptzan; Hwa Mei Trading Corporation
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks a two- or three-month commercial visit to buy goods and reorganize the company’s Japanese office.
subfiles.summary: Kaptzan describes earlier residence and business in Japan and Dairen and plans to visit principal Japanese cities.

subfiles.title: Clearance telegram for Kunsung S. Rie
subfiles.about: Authorizes Rie’s entry and instructs the embassy to issue a certified copy of the telegram.
subfiles.summary: Rie may enter between October 25, 1949, and April 25, 1950, with two photographs.

subfiles.title: Request for Albert Hamway’s travel documentation
subfiles.about: Requests proof of travel and onward-entry documents before issuance of Hamway’s permit.
subfiles.summary: Hamway is asked to provide document numbers, issuers, validity dates, and related details.

subfiles.title: Application of Albert Hamway to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks a six-month trip to purchase Japanese goods.
subfiles.summary: Hamway provides corporate, banking, and prewar trade information and proposes visiting Tokyo, Yokohama, Osaka, Nagoya, and Kobe.

subfiles.title: Entry action slip for Kunsung S. Rie
subfiles.about: Records Rie’s clearance and entry period for Japan.
subfiles.summary: The partially damaged slip records an October 25–April 25 clearance and passport-photograph requirement.

subfiles.title: Application of Kunsung S. Rie to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Kunsung S. Rie; Block International Corporation
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks a one- or two-month visit to develop two-way U.S.–Japan trade.
subfiles.summary: Rie proposes traveling from Seoul by ship to investigate imports and visit Tokyo, Osaka, Nagoya, and Kyoto.

subfiles.title: Commerce list of Superintendence and Glasbery applicants
subfiles.from: Department of Commerce, Far Eastern Branch
subfiles.about: Lists five Commerce-approved applicants for final SCAP review.
subfiles.summary: Names Azik and Henry Glasbery, Egon Arnoti, Samuel Jelin, and Lothaire Seulberger-Simon.

subfiles.title: Action slip declining Army handling of Aslaksen and Dahl
subfiles.about: Directs the Norwegian inspectors to seek assistance from Norway’s diplomatic mission.
subfiles.summary: The Army declines their applications because Norway has diplomatic representation in Japan.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum concerning M. E. Kaptzan
subfiles.about: Records Kaptzan’s identity document and U.S. re-entry permit details.
subfiles.summary: O’Brien agrees to send the information to the Pacific Military Permit Branch.

subfiles.title: Registered-mail routing instruction for Kaptzan letter
subfiles.about: Orders the underlying Kaptzan letter sent by registered mail.
subfiles.summary: Internal mailing instruction for Kaptzan’s permit letter.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Military Permit No. 5356 to M. E. Kaptzan
subfiles.about: Sends Kaptzan’s commercial-entry permit and explains the exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: Permit No. 5356 allows indefinite entry between October 27, 1949, and April 27, 1950.

subfiles.title: Submission of Kaptzan’s re-entry information
subfiles.about: Provides Kaptzan’s identity-document and U.S. re-entry-permit information.
subfiles.summary: Chappell requests issuance and return of Kaptzan’s military permit if the documentation is sufficient.

subfiles.title: George A. Mahoff’s inquiry about Anna Slenkina and V. N. Shepitkovsky
subfiles.about: Requests information and assistance concerning two relatives seeking immigration to the United States.
subfiles.summary: Mahoff says his mother had U.S. and Soviet exit visas and passage through Japan but had not been heard from since June. He also asks how his aunt’s expired preference status might be restored and requests a cable to Dairen.

subfiles.title: Air-mail envelope for Mahoff’s inquiry
subfiles.to: E. J. Madill, Department of State
subfiles.about: Envelope addressed to the Division of Protective Services.
subfiles.summary: Air-mail envelope accompanying Mahoff’s immigration inquiry.

subfiles.title: Visa Division reply to George A. Mahoff
subfiles.about: Reports Slenkina’s departure and explains the new petition required for Shepitkovsky.
subfiles.summary: The Department says Anna Slenkina has left Dairen. Because the Dairen consulate is closed and no renewed petition has arrived from Justice, Larson should file promptly and later identify the consular office where Shepitkovsky can apply.

subfiles.title: Submission of Albert Hamway’s re-entry information
subfiles.about: Provides Hamway’s identity-document and U.S. re-entry information for permit issuance.
subfiles.summary: Hamway plans to return to the United States and holds a Justice Department re-entry permit valid through February 1950.

subfiles.title: Telephone memorandum concerning Albert Hamway
subfiles.about: Records Hamway’s identity document and U.S. re-entry permit status.
subfiles.summary: O’Brien promises to request Hamway’s military permit if the information suffices.

subfiles.title: Entry action slip for Joseph I. Goldman
subfiles.about: Grants Goldman conditional commercial-entry clearance from Cairo.
subfiles.summary: Clearance requires photographs, a valid travel document, and re-entry permission outside Japan.

subfiles.title: Clearance telegram for Joseph I. Goldman
subfiles.about: Authorizes Goldman’s entry and issuance of a certified telegram copy.
subfiles.summary: Goldman may enter between October 28, 1949, and April 28, 1950, with two photographs.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Albert Hamway’s military permit
subfiles.about: Sends Hamway’s permit and notes the blanket U.S. exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: Permit No. 5374 authorizes indefinite entry between November 1, 1949, and May 1, 1950.

subfiles.title: Commerce list of Shvetz, Fattal, and another applicant
subfiles.from: Department of Commerce, Far Eastern Branch
subfiles.about: Forwards three Commerce-approved travel cases for final SCAP consideration.
subfiles.summary: The legible applicants include Alexander E. Shvetz and Violet Fattal.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Military Permit No. 5513 to Egon Arnoti
subfiles.about: Sends Arnoti’s permit and explains the blanket U.S. exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: Permit No. 5513 allows indefinite entry between November 16, 1949, and May 16, 1950.

subfiles.title: Damaged action slip concerning Superintendence Company travel
subfiles.about: Requests travel-document and onward-entry information before permits can cover the applicants’ travel.
subfiles.summary: Names are illegible, but the slip concerns conditional commercial-entry processing.

subfiles.title: Application of Egon Jules Simon Arnoti to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Egon Jules Simon Arnoti; Superintendence Company
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks a long-term assignment inspecting merchandise shipped to or from Japan.
subfiles.summary: Arnoti would work from Kobe while traveling to other Japanese cities and ports for inspection, sampling, weighing, loading, and discharge supervision.

subfiles.title: Entry action slip for Lothaire Seulberger-Simon
subfiles.about: Grants conditional indefinite commercial-entry clearance to Seulberger-Simon.
subfiles.summary: The Switzerland-based applicant needs photographs, a valid travel document, and onward-entry permission.

subfiles.title: Application of Lothaire Seulberger-Simon to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks assignment to inspect and supervise merchandise moving through Japan.
subfiles.summary: The French applicant would travel from Geneva, work principally at Kobe, and visit other Japanese cities and ports for about a year.

subfiles.title: Transmittal of Military Permit No. 5512 to Samuel Jelin
subfiles.about: Sends Jelin’s Japan-entry permit and notes the blanket exit-permit waiver.
subfiles.summary: Permit No. 5512 authorizes an indefinite stay after entry through May 16, 1950.

subfiles.title: Entry action slip for Samuel Jelin
subfiles.about: Damaged slip records conditional processing of Jelin’s commercial-entry case.
subfiles.summary: Clearance depended on satisfactory travel and onward-entry documentation.

subfiles.title: Application of Samuel Jelin to visit Japan
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Seeks a long-term assignment supervising and inspecting merchandise in Japan.
subfiles.summary: The Polish employee plans to travel by air, work chiefly from Kobe, and visit other Japanese cities and ports as needed.

subfiles.title: Request for permits for Arnoti, Jelin, and Seulberger-Simon
subfiles.about: Forwards the company’s documentation and requests completion of three entry clearances.
subfiles.summary: Chappell requests permit documents for Arnoti and Jelin but only a clearance memorandum for Seulberger-Simon, who will be notified through Geneva.

subfiles.title: Request to Superintendence Company for travel-document details
subfiles.from: Department of State, Division of Protective Services
subfiles.about: Requests documentation needed to issue permits to three company employees.
subfiles.summary: The company must supply travel-document and onward-entry details for Arnoti, Jelin, and Seulberger-Simon; Geneva will receive the latter’s cable clearance.

subfiles.title: Group action slip for Glasbery, Arnoti, and Jelin
subfiles.about: Records theater clearance for four commercial entrants, subject to travel documentation.
subfiles.summary: Covers Azik and Henry Glasbery, Egon Arnoti, and Samuel Jelin.

subfiles.title: Application of Azik Leopold and Henry Glasbery to visit Japan
subfiles.from: Azik Leopold Glasbery and Henry Glasbery; A. L. Glasbery
subfiles.to: Departments of Commerce and State; SCAP
subfiles.about: Begins an application to purchase curios in Japan for the family firm.
subfiles.summary: First page identifies the Egyptian owner, French associate, firm structure, and purchasing purpose.
